cards.text: Jesus has been with the crowds in Jerusalem, and now the story steps back to take a look at them. He has performed so many signs right in front of them. Not a rumor in the group chat, friend. RIGHT in front of them.

cards.question: After all those signs right in front of them, the people believe in Jesus.

cards.text: Then the story reaches back to Isaiah the prophet, who asked, “Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?” Friend, I've asked that first question after every joke I've ever told.

cards.question: The story says those words from Isaiah the prophet are fulfilled. Fulfilled by what?

answers.text: The people not believing in Jesus
The Greeks asking to see Jesus

cards.text: So they were unable to believe, and Isaiah says it again: “He has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts,” so they can't see with their eyes, understand with their hearts, or turn.

cards.question: In Isaiah's words, if the people could see, understand and turn, they would be healed.
The story says Isaiah said these things because he saw Jesus' ___ and spoke about Him.

cards.text: Now hold on. HOLD ON. Back up the dough truck, friend, because many of the leaders believe in Him. The LEADERS!

cards.question: The leaders who believe in Jesus confess Him out loud for everyone to hear.
Those believing leaders keep quiet because of the Pharisees, a strict Jewish religious group. What are the leaders afraid of?

answers.text: Being put out of the synagogue
Losing their seats at the feast

cards.question: The story tells why those leaders keep quiet. What do they love more than praise from God?

cards.text: Then Jesus cries out. Not a whisper, not a mumble, friend. He CRIES OUT, and it's about believing in Him.

cards.question: Jesus says whoever believes in Him doesn't believe in Him alone. Who else do they believe in?
Jesus says whoever sees Him sees the One who sent Him.

cards.text: Then Jesus says He has come into the world as a light. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, friend, so nobody has to explain to ME why that matters.

cards.question: Jesus came into the world as a light so that no one who believes in Him should remain in ___.

cards.text: Now Jesus talks about anyone who hears His words and doesn't keep them. That's hearing the oven timer go off and staying right there on the couch.

cards.question: Jesus says He judges anyone who hears His words and doesn't keep them.
Jesus says He did not come to judge the world. What did He come to do?

cards.text: But there IS a judge for the one who rejects Jesus and doesn't receive His words. And the judging comes on the last day.

cards.question: On the last day, what does Jesus say will judge the one who rejects Him?

cards.text: Jesus says He has not spoken on His own. Me? I speak on my own ALL day, and the dough has heard things it can't unhear.

cards.question: Jesus hasn't spoken on His own. Who has commanded Him what to say and how to say it?

cards.text: And Jesus knows the Father's command leads to eternal life.

cards.question: So Jesus speaks ___ what the Father has told Him to say.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: "Jesus has been with the crowds…", "He has performed so many signs…", "Not a rumor in the group chat, friend." and "RIGHT in front of them."

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: "Jesus has been with the crowds in Jerusalem" is a fact from earlier in John 12, before the passage starts. The card gives it no reference and cites only John 12:37.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "Isaiah says it again" says Isaiah repeats the same thing. In verse 39, "For again, Isaiah says" brings in a second, different quote, so the card says something the text shows is untrue.

rule.text: Noticing. What he points out must be true. "Same words" means an exact match.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: "Now hold on.", "HOLD ON.", "Back up the dough truck, friend, because many of the leaders believe in Him." and "The LEADERS!"

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup card is pure celebration ("The LEADERS!") and gives no hint that these leaders hold back. A thoughtful baker would reason their way to True, but the right answer is False. The baker can only get it right by luck.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The question asks what they love more than "praise from God." Only the right answer, "Praise from people," is a kind of praise, and it repeats the question's wording. The wrong answers are places and gold, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: "Then Jesus cries out.", "Not a whisper, not a mumble, friend." and "He CRIES OUT, and it's about believing in Him."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
